decisions.statement: Reuse the repository's task manifest and event ledgers for approval and execution; TODO documents remain source inputs and do not form a second task system.

manifest.description: Introduce a lightweight, explicit boundary between TODO/research inputs and approved implementation slices.

lifecycle.commit_reason: The implementation commit is published on docs/todo-lifecycle; PR #8 is open and merge remains out of scope.

plan.approval: Plan r5 is approved by the Orchestrator under the existing user request. It resolves the provenance finding without changing scope; QA-05 and Reviewer-04 passed on the current content revision.

skipped_phases.reason: The task is a bounded documentation contract; the approved user prompt and this manifest define the semantics, while the implementation keeps the existing repository task ledger.
Only a small local metadata validator will be considered after checking for an existing equivalent.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Canonical documentation explicitly distinguishes research input, backlog, active task, and implemented behavior and says presence in todos/ does not authorize implementation.
The chosen metadata model distinguishes review maturity from disposition and explains each allowed value.
The lifecycle covers intake, review/research, disposition, optional approved slice, implementation, and evidence; todos/ is explicitly non-FIFO.
All six named inputs have accurate kind/status/disposition metadata, with derived work linked only where traceable; substantive source text remains intact.
Any added validation is local, deterministic, and proportionate; metadata validation passes and no obsolete-behavior assertions are introduced.

constraints: Do not modify code owned by PR #6 or the execution backend, security, cost-eval, or private Control-Plane lanes.
Do not turn an input disposition into implementation approval.
Preserve all existing source text and existing detailed task gates.
non_goals: workflow engine, issue tracker, database, runtime state machine, scheduler, or automatic promotion agent
specification.objective: Preserve design and research inputs while making clear that only an approved task slice authorizes implementation.

requirements.statement: A document's presence under todos/ never grants implementation authority.
Intake status and disposition are separate, small, explicit metadata dimensions.
An approved implementation slice is recorded in the existing task manifest and task-event ledger.
The lifecycle documentation states that todos/ is not FIFO and defines the evidence path.
Current named research inputs receive metadata consistent with known evidence, without changing their substantive content.

concepts.meaning: A durable design or research document kept for consideration; it is not an implementation authorization.
How far an input has progressed through intake and review, independently of its disposition.
The current decision about an input's handling; it does not itself authorize code changes.
An implementation unit recorded as approved work through the repository's task manifest and task-event ledger.
Behavior present in code or configuration and backed by task-linked validation evidence.

invariants.statement: A TODO/research input and its disposition never authorize implementation; an approved slice must be recorded in the canonical task state.
An implemented behavior claim is linked to its approved task and evidence; a source input is not labeled wholly implemented when only part was adopted.

semantic_model.scope: Repository records and implementation authority for design and research inputs.
